title: Daniell cell
back: Zn anode (−) is oxidised; Cu cathode (+) is reduced. Electrons flow Zn → Cu; the salt bridge keeps both halves neutral.

title: Electrolytic cell (molten NaCl)
back: The battery forces a non-spontaneous change. Anode (+): $\ce{2Cl- -> Cl2 + 2e-}$. Cathode (−): $\ce{Na+ + e- -> Na}$.

title: Standard cell potential
legend: E^\circ_\text{cathode} = reduction potential of the right (+) electrode
E^\circ_\text{anode} = reduction potential of the left (−) electrode
back: In words: right minus left, both as **reduction** potentials. Never multiply $E^\circ$ by a coefficient. Daniell: $0.34-(-0.76)=1.10$ V.

title: Nernst equation (298 K)
legend: n = electrons transferred in the balanced cell reaction
back: In words: the voltage falls as products pile up. Leave solids out of $Q$; read $n$ and $Q$ off the balanced cell reaction.

title: Gibbs energy and K from E°
legend: F = 96 500 C mol⁻¹ (one mole of electrons)
\Delta_rG^\circ = in J mol⁻¹, divide by 1000 for kJ
back: In words: positive $E^\circ$ means negative $\Delta G^\circ$, a spontaneous reaction. A dead cell is at equilibrium ($E=0$, $Q=K_c$).

title: Conductivity and molar conductivity
legend: \Lambda_m = S cm² mol⁻¹, M in mol L⁻¹
back: In words: $\Lambda_m$ is the conducting power of the ions from **one mole**. The 1000 works only with $\kappa$ in S cm⁻¹.

title: Λm against √c: strong vs weak
back: Strong (KCl): straight line, extrapolate to read $\Lambda_m^\circ$. Weak ($\ce{CH3COOH}$): steep rise at low $c$, cannot be extrapolated, so use Kohlrausch.

title: Kohlrausch's law
legend: \nu_\pm = number of each ion in the formula
back: In words: at infinite dilution each ion moves on its own. $\Lambda^\circ_{\ce{CH3COOH}}=\Lambda^\circ_{\ce{CH3COONa}}+\Lambda^\circ_{\ce{HCl}}-\Lambda^\circ_{\ce{NaCl}}$; then $\alpha=\Lambda_m/\Lambda_m^\circ$.

title: Faraday's first law
legend: I\,t = charge Q in coulombs (t in seconds!)
n = electrons per ion (Ag⁺ 1, Cu²⁺ 2, Al³⁺ 3)
F = 96 500 C per mole of electrons
back: In words: one mole of electrons is one faraday. Convert minutes to seconds before anything else.

title: Lead storage battery (discharge)
back: Sulphuric acid is used up and water forms, so the density falls. Recharging reverses the reaction.

title: H₂–O₂ fuel cell
back: Anode (top) and cathode (bottom) in hot aqueous KOH or NaOH; about 70% efficient; product is water.

title: Rusting is electrochemical
back: Iron is the anode, oxygen is reduced at the cathode; rust is Fe₂O₃·xH₂O. Zinc or magnesium protect iron as sacrificial anodes.
